sections.title: PART A · Section A: Reading. Answer in ONE word.

questions.q: Where, according to Gandhiji, does the real India live?
On what did Gandhiji encourage people to spin khadi?
What must education build, according to Gandhiji?

sections.passage:
Mahatma Gandhi believed that the real India lives in its villages. He dreamt of villages that were clean, self-reliant and full of cottage industries. He encouraged people to spin khadi on the charkha so that every home could earn some money and depend less on foreign goods.
Gandhiji also stressed cleanliness. He himself cleaned toilets in his ashram and taught others that no work is low or dirty. He felt that a clean village would also be a healthy village, free from many diseases.
Education was another of his concerns. His idea of 'basic education' meant that children should learn through useful crafts like weaving, gardening and carpentry, and should also learn to respect manual labour. He believed that education must build character, not just fill the mind with facts.
Today many of these ideas are coming back in new forms. Campaigns for cleanliness, skill training and support for local products show that Gandhiji's vision of a self-reliant India is still alive.

sections.passage:
Yoga is an ancient Indian practice that joins the body, mind and breath. The word 'yoga' comes from the Sanskrit word 'yuj', which means 'to unite'. Today people all over the world practise it, and since 2015 the United Nations has celebrated 21 June as International Day of Yoga.
Regular yoga makes the body flexible and strong. Asanas, or postures, stretch the muscles and improve balance. Pranayama, or breathing exercises, increases the supply of oxygen and calms the nerves. Meditation helps people concentrate and reduces stress, anger and anxiety.
Doctors say that yoga can help people with problems like back pain, high blood pressure and sleeplessness. Students who practise yoga often find that they remember lessons better and feel less nervous before examinations.
However, yoga should be learnt from a trained teacher. Some postures can cause injury if done wrongly or too quickly. Yoga is best done on an empty stomach, in fresh air, and with patience, because its benefits grow slowly over time.

sections.title: Section B: Writing. Answer in 150–200 words.

questions.q: You are Riya of Class X. Write an article (150–200 words) on 'Mobile Phones: A Boon or a Bane for Students'. Clues: easy communication — online learning — information at fingertips — addiction and wasted time — effects on eyes and sleep — cyber dangers — balanced use.
questions.answer: Points: title and by-line; introduction; boon — contact with family, online classes and study material, quick information, safety; bane — addiction, less study and outdoor play, eye strain and poor sleep, harmful content and cyber crime; conclusion — a mobile is a good servant but a bad master; use it wisely with limits and parental guidance. 150–200 words in paragraphs.

or.q: You are Arif. Write a report (150–200 words) for your school magazine on the Annual Sports Day held in your school.
or.answer: Points: heading, by-line, date and venue; chief guest and inauguration (lighting of the torch, march past); main events — races, relay, long jump, tug of war; winners and the champion house; cultural items; prize distribution and speech; conclusion on the spirit of sportsmanship. Past tense, factual style.

sections.title: Answer in about 100 words.

questions.q: You are Nikhil of 8, Civil Lines, Jaipur. Write a letter (about 100 words) to your friend congratulating him on winning the first prize in a state-level painting competition.
questions.answer: Format: address, date, 'Dear Rahul'. Body: joy on hearing the news; praise for his talent and hard work; recalling his love of painting; wishing him greater success; asking about the prize-winning painting. Closing 'Yours lovingly, Nikhil'. Informal and warm.

or.q: You are Meera of 3, Hill View, Shimla. Write a letter (about 100 words) to the Manager, City Book Store, Delhi, placing an order for some English story books for your school library.
or.answer: Format of a formal letter: sender's address, date, receiver's address, subject (Order for story books), 'Sir/Madam'. Body: list of books with authors and number of copies; mode of payment; request for timely delivery and discount. Closing 'Yours faithfully, Meera, Librarian/Student Secretary'.

questions.q: What was the son's opinion about his father's work, and how did it differ from his father's view? (The Last Stone Mason)
questions.answer: Gopal thought the work was useless because it did not pay and had brought them only poverty; he wanted to mass produce goods for tourists. His father believed money alone did not matter — carving statues for temples was a service to God and a family tradition of hundreds of years.

or.q: Describe the character of the old stone mason.
or.answer: He was a dedicated, devout artist who saw his work as service to God. He was gentle even with his angry son, proud of his family tradition, hardworking — working till he fainted — and generous in recognising Salim's talent, calling him his son.
